                                    <condition>
                                        <and>

                                            <not><isset property="pathland.native.host.present" /></not>
                                        </and>
                                    </condition>

Hosts any number of them. - **`PathlandHost`** — the multi-app dispatcher: one `PathlandRegistry` per mounted app (own actor thread, own sessions). `match(requestUri)` resolves the owning registry by **longest mount-prefix match** and reports the **mount-stripped route** (a root mount claims every unclaimed path). The SSR request therefore has no `wid`: `renderHtml(route, wid)` with a null `wid` renders defaults; the client's live session is scoped by the WS `wid`, and a same-tab reload re-syncs that window's persisted state over the WebSocket. The old `session` cookie is removed. - **`PathlandSession`** — per-session: builds the `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` signal, mounts `app.newRoot().modifiers(environmentBinding(e -> e.key(ACTIVE_PATH).value(activePath)))`, **delta-batched send-on-`endFrame`** (`DeltaBatcher` coalesces per-signal frames into one batch — flush ~20 ms or 16 KB, string offsets rebased — so a continuous input burst can't overflow a remote WebSocket send queue), `applyEnvironment` (re-route guard-aware via the bound router), `dispatch` (tap/nav-intent/text/value/date/NAVIGATE), `resync`, `renderHtml`, `close`. Now takes the app's `base` and `stateScope` explicitly (the registry supplies them). - **`DeltaBatcher`** — merges session delta frames (opcodes + a single rebased string section) and flushes as one network batch on a timer/byte threshold; the Java analogue of the Rust transport's `Batcher`. It owns the per-session **message sequence** (stamped on each flushed batch via `FrameCodec.encodeFrame(frame, sequence)`) so the DOM client can detect a lost batch and recover with `META::RESYNC` (spec/OPCODE.md §Sequence gap detection); an empty flush consumes no sequence. The **sender runs OUTSIDE the monitor** — a blocking/queueing send can never stall the actor thread's `append` or the flush scheduler. Coalescing tests cover merging + rebasing, a 100-frame burst collapsing to one send, incrementing sequences, and a blocking sender not holding the lock. - **`PathlandConnection`** — the transport seam (`send(byte[])`/`isOpen()`); each starter adapts its WebSocket type to it. - **Observability seam** — `PathlandTelemetry` (default `NOOP`): the runtime emits session open/close, inbound event batches, flushed batches (frames/opcodes/bytes + merge-encode time), SSR render latency, resync requests, and send failures; the host binds a pull-based active-sessions gauge. `PathlandHost`/`PathlandRegistry`/ `PathlandSession`/`DeltaBatcher` thread it through (a host with no telemetry pays nothing). `pathland-observability` provides the Micrometer + OpenTelemetry adapters; the starters auto-wire them. Logging is **SLF4J** (both frameworks bind it) — the old ad-hoc `System.out` is gone. See issue #62. - **Concurrency stress** — `RegistryConcurrencyTest`: 100 sessions driven through the registry concurrently (clicks on each session's button) while SSR-style requests construct throwaway sessions on request threads — the shared-actor / global-`Scheduler` cross-session corruption guard. The content-hashed name busts the immutable asset cache with a fresh URL per build. The built-in base design is linked the same way: `renderHtml` renders through `HtmlRenderer.renderLinked(frame, root, base)`, so the CSS href is `{base}/base-.css` (token overrides/fit rules stay inline). # pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 28, 2026

The **Java binding to the Rust HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a
thin **JNA shim** over `libpathland_render_html`. There is a **single renderer**

  `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a self-contained snapshot frame to
  HTML in one pass (no retained tree, no `applyFrame`); `pathland_html_free`
  releases native strings. Lazy-loaded; skipped (test assumption) when the dylib
  is absent from `java.library.path`.

  bind the Rust `pathland_html_render_debug` exports — each rendered node is
  prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers
  applied (opt-in; the plain `render` output is unchanged).

# pathland-view-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

The sole JVM authoring surface (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`), Kotlin-owned over the
Kotlin `pathland-view-core`. The Java DSL, its processor, and its Java-only
Quarkus extension/starter alias are removed.

## Authoring surface

- **Kotlin-owned**: all primitives, shapes, stacks, grids, scroll/lazy

  `Label`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`, `ProxyView`, styles (`PlainButtonStyle`,
  `BorderedButtonStyle`, label styles, `NativeVideoStyle`), and the complete
  modifier vocabulary (padding/frame/fonts/colors/borders/shadows/effects/
  transforms/interaction/accessibility/environment/styles/window metadata).
- **Dependency boundary**: main depends on `pathland-view-core` only.
- Tests are Kotlin-only; golden engine traces and opcode/property assertions
  replace the former Java-vs-Kotlin parity oracle.

## Implemented

- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`, `Rectangle`,
  `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`,
  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.

  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
  `ProxyView`.
- **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
  `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
  `ColorPicker`.
- **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no

  `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`, `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
- **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
  layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,

=== test-kit status
# Pathland Test Kit

Shared test infrastructure for the Pathland Java reactor.

## Implemented

- **`dev.pathland.server.test.WsSession`** — a minimal JDK-`java.net.http.WebSocket`
  client that speaks the PLPL wire protocol (environment / resync / click / ping),
  collects decoded frames + peer-close codes, and tracks unexpected closes. One shared
  `HttpClient` across all connections.
- **`dev.pathland.server.test.MultiSessionProbe`** — the shared 100-session (configurable
  via `PATHLAND_TEST_SESSIONS`) WS stress probe used by the Quarkus + Spring starters'
  `MultiSessionWebSocketTest`: every session connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level
  PONGs, stays isolated (only its own click counts reach its label), and is never closed
  by the peer.

The harness lives in **main scope** so `mvn package` (the Docker/Render build, which runs
`-Dmaven.test.skip=true`) resolves it as a normal jar — a `tests`-classifier test-jar
dependency previously broke the package build. The starters depend on this module with
`scope=test`.

## Verified by

The starters' `MultiSessionWebSocketTest` runs (both green in `mvn clean install`); the
full Docker image build (`docker build -f lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile .`)
succeeds.=== observability status
# pathland-observability — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 3, 2026

Observability adapters for the framework-agnostic `pathland-server-core`
telemetry seam. The core emits lifecycle/throughput events through
`PathlandTelemetry` (default `NOOP`); this module turns them into metrics and
spans. Protocol/contract context: `spec/OPCODE.md`; the seam itself is in
`pathland-server-core`.

## Implemented

- **`MicrometerTelemetry`** — a `PathlandTelemetry` over any Micrometer
  `MeterRegistry` (Prometheus, OTLP, …). Metric catalog:
  - `pathland.sessions.active` — gauge (pull-based, bound by the host)
  - `pathland.sessions.opened` / `pathland.sessions.closed` — counters
  - `pathland.events.received` — counter (decoded inbound events)
  - `pathland.batches.sent` / `pathland.frames.sent` / `pathland.bytes.sent` — counters
  - `pathland.batch.size` — distribution summary (opcodes per batch)
  - `pathland.batch.flush` — timer (merge + encode)
  - `pathland.ssr.render` — timer (SSR render round-trip)
  - `pathland.resync.requested` — counter
  - `pathland.ws.failures` — counter
  - Every meter is tagged by `mount` (bounded). Registrations are idempotent, so
    a builder per event is cheap and cannot leak meters.
- **`TracingTelemetry`** — an OpenTelemetry decorator over another
  `PathlandTelemetry`: emits a span per frame send (`pathland.frame.send`), per
  inbound event batch (`pathland.event.batch`), and per SSR render
  (`pathland.ssr.render`), with the wrapped telemetry still receiving every
  event. Spans are back-dated by the measured duration so they render with the
  real latency. Opt-in — the starters build it only when a `Tracer`/`OpenTelemetry`
  bean is available.

## Not implemented / gaps

- No client-side (browser) telemetry — server-side only.
- `ws.failures` does not tag the failure reason (unbounded cardinality).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-observability` — `MicrometerTelemetryTest` (the full
metric catalog + per-mount tagging) and `TracingTelemetryTest` (span names via an
in-memory OTel exporter, plus delegation). The starters' tests assert the wiring
end to end (`/q/health` + `/q/metrics`, `/actuator/health` + `pathland.*` meters).

## Maven module dependency walkthrough

**19 reactor modules** — 12 published library/extension artifacts + 7 non-published demo modules.

### Actual dependency graph

```
pathland-view-core                        (engine, protocol, signals, state, transport; Kotlin)
├── pathland-view-kotlin                  (authoring DSL)
├── pathland-render-html                  (JNA shim → Rust renderer)
│   └── pathland-server-core
│       ├── pathland-observability        (Micrometer/OTel adapters)
│       ├── pathland-spring-boot-starter  (server-core + observability + Spring)
│       └── pathland-quarkus              (server-core + observability + Quarkus)
│           ├── pathland-quarkus-deployment            (build-time)
│           └── pathland-quarkus-kotlin  (0 code: deps + descriptor)
│               └── pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment (build-time)
├── pathland-state-redis                  (Lettuce StateStore)
└── pathland-test-kit                     (WsSession / MultiSessionProbe)

pathland-demo-common (theme + 24 assets)
└── pathland-demo-views-kotlin (MusicPlayerView, AdView)
    ├── pathland-gtk-demo
    ├── pathland-qt-demo
    ├── pathland-quarkus-demo         (+ pathland-quarkus, demo-common)
    ├── pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo  (+ pathland-quarkus-kotlin, view-kotlin)
    └── pathland-spring-boot-demo     (+ spring-boot-starter, demo-common)
```

### Findings / candidates

**Clear win (low risk, demos only, nothing published):**
- `pathland-demo-common` is a 3-file module (theme + assets) used by all 5 host demos, and every host demo already depends on `pathland-demo-views-kotlin`. Merging `demo-common` into `demo-views-kotlin` removes one module with zero API impact.
- Demos are half the reactor (7 of 19) and force Spring/Quarkus/Kotlin/JNA into every library build. They could be gated behind a `-Pdemos` profile (or a separate aggregator) so `mvn install` builds the 12 library modules only.

**Real dependency smell (not a merge, but worth fixing):**
- `pathland-server-core` has a **hard compile dependency on `pathland-state-redis`** (`server-core/StateStores.java:22`), so every Spring/Quarkus app transitively ships Lettuce even when it never uses Redis. Better: move `StateStores.redisOrFallback` into the starters (or discover `StateStoreProvider` via `ServiceLoader`) and let consumers opt into `pathland-state-redis`. Keep it a separate module.
- `server-core → render-html` is hard, but legitimate (SSR); it already degrades via `HtmlRenderer.tryInstance()`. Leave it.

**Not worth merging:**
- `view-core` + `view-kotlin`: both Kotlin, but the split preserves the DSL-neutral engine boundary; merging forces the DSL on engine-only consumers.
- `observability` → `server-core`: only saves one small artifact but drags Micrometer/OTel into the core dependency surface.
- `quarkus-kotlin` (no code) → `quarkus`: would force Kotlin onto Java-only hosts, breaking the DSL-neutral extension design.
- `quarkus-kotlin-deployment` → `quarkus-deployment`: would drag `quarkus-kotlin-deployment` into every Java Quarkus build; Quarkus' runtime/deployment artifact split is required anyway.
- `render-html` → `server-core`: loses the standalone HTML binding and adds the Rust build to the core artifact.
- `test-kit` → `view-core`/`server-core`: only 2 files, but its main-scope jar is deliberately separate (a test-jar broke the Docker package build).

**Minor duplication:** `RingEventReader` is essentially duplicated between `gtk-demo` and `qt-demo`; could live in the demo support module rather than be merged.

### Recommendation

Keep all 12 published artifacts as-is (they encode meaningful boundaries), and do two things:
1. Merge `pathland-demo-common` into `pathland-demo-views-kotlin`.
2. Decouple `server-core` from `state-redis` (optional/ServiceLoader), and gate demos out of the default library build.

Which scope do you want me to turn into an execution plan?

content.text:
Given nothing is published, I'd consolidate more aggressively. Here's the target I recommend.

## Target module graph (19 → 10)

**Before**
```
view-core ← view-kotlin            (both Kotlin, DSL depends on engine)
view-core ← state-redis ─┐
view-core ← render-html ─┼→ server-core ← observability
view-core ← test-kit ────┘
server-core + observability → spring-boot-starter
server-core + observability → quarkus ← quarkus-kotlin (0 code)
                                ├ quarkus-deployment ← quarkus-kotlin-deployment (0 code)
demo-common ← demo-views-kotlin ← {gtk, qt, quarkus, spring, quarkus-kotlin} demos
```

**After (6 published + 4 demo)**
```
pathland-view-core       = view-core + view-kotlin (engine + sole Kotlin DSL)
pathland-render-html     = unchanged (standalone JNA binding)
pathland-server-core     = server-core + state-redis + observability + test-kit
pathland-spring-boot-starter
pathland-quarkus         = quarkus + quarkus-kotlin (runtime)
pathland-quarkus-deployment = quarkus-deployment + quarkus-kotlin-deployment

pathland-demo-views-kotlin (or pathland-demo) = demo-common + demo-views-kotlin
pathland-desktop-demo    = gtk-demo + qt-demo
pathland-quarkus-demo    = keep (optionally absorb the Kotlin demo)
pathland-spring-boot-demo = keep
```

## Merge details

**1. `view-kotlin` → `view-core`**
Both are already Kotlin; packages (`dev.pathland.view.core.*` / `.engine.*` / `.dsl.*`) don't collide. Keep the surviving artifactId `pathland-view-core` — do **not** rename to `pathland-view`, because the root enforcer explicitly bans `dev.pathland:pathland-view` (old Java DSL, `pom.xml:120`). Move sources/tests, merge the Kotlin plugin + surefire config, drop the self-dependency.

**2. `state-redis` + `observability` + `test-kit` → `server-core`**
- `StateStores.java:22` already hard-references `RedisStateStore`, so Lettuce is currently a mandatory transitive dep. Merging makes that explicit and removes the odd edge rather than pretending it's optional.
- Observability is 2 files over `server-core`'s `PathlandTelemetry`; keep Micrometer compile and OTel optional.
- `test-kit` is 2 main-scope files; folding it into `dev.pathland.server.test` removes the artifact while preserving the "main jar so `-Dmaven.test.skip=true` resolves it" property. (Tradeoff: test utilities ship in the runtime jar. Keeping it separate is the one defensible holdout.)

**3. `quarkus-kotlin` → `quarkus`, `quarkus-kotlin-deployment` → `quarkus-deployment`**
- `quarkus-kotlin` has zero sources — only `pathland-view-kotlin` + `quarkus-kotlin` deps and a descriptor. Add both deps to `pathland-quarkus`, and list both capabilities (`dev.pathland.quarkus`, `dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin`).
- Merge `PathlandKotlinProcessor`'s `FeatureBuildItem("pathland-kotlin")` into `PathlandProcessor`, add `quarkus-kotlin-deployment` to the deployment pom, delete both Kotlin modules.
- Caveat: this makes every Quarkus user pull `quarkus-kotlin`. Fine now that Kotlin is the only JVM DSL; if Java-only hosts matter later, re-split.

**4. Demos**
- `demo-common` → `demo-views-kotlin`: all 5 host demos already depend on the views module, so `DemoTheme`/`DemoAssets` become transitive. Delete `demo-common` + its `status.md`.
- `gtk-demo` + `qt-demo` → `pathland-desktop-demo`: both are JNA hosts over the same views; keep two packages and dedupe the duplicated `RingEventReader` (gtk Java 116 lines vs qt Kotlin 101 lines). Use exec profiles for each renderer.
- `quarkus-kotlin-demo`: likely redundant now — the Java Quarkus demo already mounts Kotlin views. Either delete it or convert `KotlinDemoView` into a `/kotlin` mounted app inside `pathland-quarkus-demo`. This is the only genuinely debatable deletion.

**Do not merge**
- `render-html` into `server-core`: its antrun native-dylib embed step is a distinct build boundary; merging makes `server-core` fail without a Rust build.
- Spring and Quarkus modules: framework glue.
- Quarkus runtime and deployment must remain separate artifact pairs by Quarkus convention.

## Migration checklist

1. Move source trees/resources, merge poms, update root `<modules>`.
2. Update every internal dependency coordinate (`render-html`, `server-core`, starters, demos).
3. Update build tooling: `scripts/lib.sh`, `scripts/run-java-{gtk,qt}-demo.sh`, `run-quarkus*.sh`, `run-spring-demo.sh`, `lib/typescript/scripts/copy-to-demos.mjs`, `pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile`.
4. Update CI/release: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `release.yml` module lists and demo exclusions.
5. Update docs/status per the AGENTS mandate: `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `RELEASING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `docs/*`, and merge/delete the affected `status.md` files.
6. Verify: `cargo build -p pathland-render-html`, then `cd lib/java && mvn clean install`; targeted starter tests (`pathland-quarkus`, `pathland-spring-boot-starter`); package each demo; `git grep` for stale artifact IDs.

Safe order: demos first (unpublished), then `server-core` adapters, then `view-core`, then Quarkus.

Two choices determine whether this lands at 10 or 12 modules:

package dev.pathland.demo.quarkus.kotlin

import dev.pathland.demo.ad.AdView
import dev.pathland.demo.music.MusicPlayerView
import dev.pathland.server.MountedApp
import dev.pathland.server.PathlandApp
import dev.pathland.view.core.View
import jakarta.enterprise.context.ApplicationScoped
import jakarta.enterprise.inject.Produces
import jakarta.inject.Singleton
import org.eclipse.microprofile.config.inject.ConfigProperty

/**
 * The entire app: the DSL-neutral Quarkus extension provides SSR, the per-app
 * WebSocket endpoint, sessions and state; this bean supplies a fresh Kotlin root.
 *
 * Two apps share the server: the [MusicPlayerView] at `/` and the [AdView] at `/ad`.
 * The player's Now Playing pane embeds the ad app via a `ProxyView`
 * (spec/PROXY.md) — a same-server proxy on a loopback WebSocket.
 */
@ApplicationScoped
class KotlinDemoApplication : PathlandApp {

    /** The `/ad` app's base URL — the proxy origin. */
    @field:ConfigProperty(name = "pathland.demo.ad-url", defaultValue = "http://localhost:8080/ad")
    lateinit var adUrl: String

    override fun newRoot(): View = MusicPlayerView.make(adUrl)

    /** The origin app mounted at `/ad`: the small sponsored-proxy ad app. */
    @Produces
    @Singleton
    fun adApp(): MountedApp = MountedApp.of("/ad", PathlandApp { AdView() })
}

## Final consolidation plan (19 → 10 modules)

Decisions applied: Kotlin Quarkus demo absorbed into `pathland-quarkus-demo`; `pathland-test-kit` merged into `server-core`.

### Target

| # | Surviving module | Absorbs |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `pathland-view-core` | `pathland-view-kotlin` |
| 2 | `pathland-render-html` | — |
| 3 | `pathland-server-core` | `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-observability`, `pathland-test-kit` |
| 4 | `pathland-spring-boot-starter` | — |
| 5 | `pathland-quarkus` | `pathland-quarkus-kotlin` |
| 6 | `pathland-quarkus-deployment` | `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment` |
| 7 | `pathland-demo-views-kotlin` | `pathland-demo-common` |
| 8 | `pathland-desktop-demo` | `pathland-gtk-demo`, `pathland-qt-demo` |
| 9 | `pathland-quarkus-demo` | `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo` |
| 10 | `pathland-spring-boot-demo` | — |

Keep package names unchanged (`dev.pathland.view.core`, `.dsl`, `.server`, `.state.redis`, `.observability`, `.server.test`, `.demo.*`) so only Maven coordinates and file locations move.

### Execution order

**Phase 1 — demos (unpublished, safest)**
1. Move `demo-common`'s `DemoTheme`, `DemoAssets`, 24 assets, and test into `pathland-demo-views-kotlin`; drop its internal dep; delete `pathland-demo-common`.
2. Move `gtk-demo` + `qt-demo` into `pathland-desktop-demo`; keep `dev.pathland.demo.gtk` / `.qt` packages, add two exec executions/profiles, and dedupe the duplicated `RingEventReader`.
3. Fold `KotlinDemoApplication` into `pathland-quarkus-demo` as a `MountedApp.of("/kotlin", …)` bean (not a second `PathlandApp` bean — that would conflict). Merge its `application.properties` notes; delete the module. Delete `scripts/run-quarkus-kotlin-demo.sh` or alias it to the Quarkus demo.
4. Update `scripts/lib.sh:38`, `scripts/run-java-{gtk,qt}-demo.sh`, `lib/typescript/scripts/copy-to-demos.mjs:25-27`, `pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile:22,27`, and CI's demo-resource diff step (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:226`).

**Phase 2 — server adapters**
5. Move `RedisStateStore`, `MicrometerTelemetry`, `TracingTelemetry`, `WsSession`, `MultiSessionProbe` into `pathland-server-core`; merge pom deps (Lettuce compile, Micrometer compile, OTel optional, test-scope JUnit/OTel SDK).
6. Remove the now-redundant `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-observability`, `pathland-test-kit` deps from the starters/Quarkus; they get everything transitively from `server-core`. Delete the three modules.

**Phase 3 — view**
7. Move `pathland-view-kotlin/src/main/kotlin` + tests into `pathland-view-core`; merge Kotlin plugin config. Apply `-Xjvm-default=all` module-wide (view-core already uses it; verify view-kotlin default-method behavior).
8. Replace all `pathland-view-kotlin` coordinates with `pathland-view-core` (server-core, render-html, starters, quarkus, demos). Delete `pathland-view-kotlin`.

**Phase 4 — Quarkus**
9. Add `pathland-view-core` + `quarkus-kotlin` deps to `pathland-quarkus`; merge the two `META-INF/quarkus-extension.yaml` files and declare both capabilities (`dev.pathland.quarkus`, `dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin`).
10. Add `quarkus-kotlin-deployment` to `pathland-quarkus-deployment` and merge `PathlandKotlinProcessor`'s `FeatureBuildItem("pathland-kotlin")`. Delete both Kotlin extension modules.
11. Do **not** rename the merged view artifact to `pathland-view`: the enforcer at `lib/java/pom.xml` bans that coordinate (old Java DSL).

**Phase 5 — bookkeeping**
12. Update root `<modules>` (`lib/java/pom.xml:47-67`) and the release module list (`.github/workflows/release.yml:231-241`).
13. Merge/delete affected `status.md` files and update `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `RELEASING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `docs/*` per the mandatory status-sync rule.

### Verification
1. `cd lib/rust && cargo build -p pathland-render-html` (Java tests need the dylib).
2. `cd lib/java && mvn clean install` — full reactor.
3. Targeted: `mvn -pl pathland-quarkus,pathland-spring-boot-starter,pathland-server-core test`.
4. Package demos individually; run the desktop and web demo scripts.
5. `git grep` for every deleted artifactId to confirm no stale references.

### Risks to watch
- `pathland-quarkus` now pulls `quarkus-kotlin` for all Quarkus users (accepted, since Kotlin is the only JVM DSL).
- `server-core` becomes the runtime + adapters + test harness jar (accepted for POC; it is already the de-facto center of gravity).
- `view-core` + `view-kotlin` merge changes Kotlin compiler flags; run the full test suite, especially signal/DSL default-method tests.

No file changes were made.

# pathland-demo-views-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

Kotlin-owned demo views over `pathland-view-kotlin`, with no Java-DSL dependency.
It owns the app-driven music player and the small sponsored-proxy ad app.

## Structure

- `music/` — the root `MusicPlayerView` (public, Java-mountable).
- `music/model/` — `Track`, `Lyrics`.
- `music/library/` — `LibraryView`, `TrackRowView`.
- `music/player/` — `PlayerMainArea`, `PlayerBar`, `PlayerControls`,
  `TransportControls`, `TrackInfoView`, `VolumeControls`.
- `music/player/controls/` — `SeekControl`, `PercentSeek`, `VolumeControl`.
- `music/service/` — `MediaPlayerService`: per-session player state, playlist,
  `MediaController`, and the environment key shared by the views.
- `music/lyrics/` — `SubtitlePill`.
- `music/sidebar/` — `NowPlayingSidebar`, `UpNextRowView`.
- `ad/` — `AdView`.

## Implemented

- **`MusicPlayerView`** — Apple Music-style root: one root `SizeThatFits`
  selects narrow (no volume), medium (volume), or wide (volume + `NowPlayingSidebar`),
  with the floating `PlayerBar`.
- **Persisted player state** — owned by `MediaPlayerService` (`player.position`, `player.playing`,
  `player.track`, `player.volume`, `player.seekRequest`, `player.volumeRequest`)
  and created with `Signals.state` while the framework's session state is active.
- **App-driven media** — `MediaPlayerService` owns and registers the
  `MediaController`, and the emitter projects it as a pinned root node; every fit
  candidate shares the same controller. `MEDIA_*` reports feed position/volume
  and `MEDIA_ENDED` advances the track.
- **Seek/volume decoupling** — `SeekControl` buffers drags and commits on release;
  `PercentSeek` maps seconds to 0..100; `VolumeControl` separates report from
  command (each in its own file under `player/controls/`).
- **Lyrics** — synchronized two-line karaoke pill driven by the parsed SRT cues.
- **Window metadata** — track-derived title/description and `locale("en")`.
- **Sponsored proxy** — optional `adUrl` appends a `ProxyView` in the sidebar.
- **`AdView`** — the small sponsored-proxy origin app: a title, a button, and a
  persisted click counter (`ad.clicks`), fully Kotlin-owned and Java-mountable.
- **Accessibility** — transport labels, slider labels, `MAIN`/`HEADER` roles.

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-demo-views-kotlin` — `LyricsTest`, `SeekControlTest`,
`MediaPlayerServiceTest` (persisted keys, select/next/previous), `MusicPlayerViewTest`
(tree/render, fit swaps, media state, seek echo guard, snapshot emission, sponsored
proxy), and `AdViewTest` (button click / persisted counter delta).

package dev.pathland.demo.qt

import com.sun.jna.Memory
import dev.pathland.demo.DemoTheme
import dev.pathland.demo.assets.DemoAssets
import dev.pathland.demo.music.MusicPlayerView
import dev.pathland.view.core.Environment
import dev.pathland.view.core.ffm.PathlandCore
import dev.pathland.view.core.ffm.RingOpcodeSink
import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signals
import dev.pathland.view.core.state.InMemoryStateStore
import dev.pathland.view.core.state.PersistentState
import dev.pathland.view.engine.Emitter
import dev.pathland.view.engine.InputDispatcher

/**
 * Runs the shared Kotlin [MusicPlayerView] under the native Qt Quick renderer.
 *
 * The Kotlin DSL mounts the view through the fine-grained [Emitter] into a
 * `libpathland_core` shared ring ([RingOpcodeSink], zero-copy). The in-process
 * Qt renderer pumps the same ring in place (`pathland_qt_run_ring`); native
 * inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that this host drains and dispatches
 * through [InputDispatcher] into the app's bindings.
 *
 * No Swing, no Qt API — only Pathland authoring.
 */
object QtHost {

    /** Max events drained per wake (× 16 bytes each). */
    private const val MAX_EVENTS = 64
    private const val WINDOW_WIDTH = 1180
    private const val WINDOW_HEIGHT = 800

    @JvmStatic
    fun main(args: Array<String>) {
        val core = PathlandCore.instance()
        RingOpcodeSink(core).use { sink ->
            val handle = sink.handle()

            // The session's state + theme, exactly as the server session seeds them.
            val state = PersistentState(InMemoryStateStore(), "desktop")
            // A placeholder host path signal: MusicPlayerView has no router.
            val activePath = Signals.signal("/")

            val emitter = Emitter(sink, DemoTheme.adaptive())
            val result = emitter.mount(MusicPlayerView.make(), Environment(state))
            val dispatcher = InputDispatcher(result, activePath)
            val reader = RingEventReader(core.ringPtr(handle), core.ringLen(handle))

            // Wake callback: drain raw EVENT opcodes and route them into the app's
            // bindings. Re-emission happens on the Qt main thread, the only writer.
            val onEvent = QtRendererNative.EventCallback {
                val buf = Memory(MAX_EVENTS.toLong() * 16)
                val n = core.drainEvents(handle, buf, MAX_EVENTS)
                if (n > 0) {
                    dispatcher.dispatch(reader.decode(buf.getByteArray(0, n * 16)))
                }
            }

            val renderer = QtRendererNative.instance()
            renderer.setAssetRoot(DemoAssets.extractToTemp().toString())

            // Blocks until the window closes; the ring (handle) must outlive it.
            renderer.runRing(core.ringMut(handle), onEvent, WINDOW_WIDTH, WINDOW_HEIGHT)
        }
    }
}

package dev.pathland.demo.qt

import com.sun.jna.Callback
import com.sun.jna.Library
import com.sun.jna.Native
import com.sun.jna.Pointer
import java.io.File
import java.util.Locale

/**
 * JNA binding to the Rust Qt renderer cdylib (`libpathland_qt`).
 *
 * The Kotlin DSL emits opcodes into a `libpathland_core` ring
 * ([dev.pathland.view.core.ffm.RingOpcodeSink]); [runRing] hands that borrowed
 * ring to the in-process Qt Quick renderer (`pathland_qt_run_ring`), which pumps
 * it in place. Native inputs are reported back through a no-payload callback;
 * the host drains them from the ring itself.
 */
class QtRendererNative private constructor() {

    /** Invoked (with no payload) on the Qt main thread after a raw input was written. */
    fun interface EventCallback : Callback {
        fun invoke()
    }

    /** The C ABI surface, mapped by JNA onto the Rust cdylib. */
    interface NativeQtRenderer : Library {
        fun pathland_qt_set_asset_root(dir: String)
        fun pathland_qt_run_ring(ring: Pointer, onEvent: EventCallback?, width: Int, height: Int)
    }

    private val nativeQt: NativeQtRenderer

    init {
        val libraryPath = resolveLibraryPath()
            ?: throw IllegalStateException(
                "libpathland_qt not found; set -Dpathland.qt.lib to its full path " +
                    "(cargo build -p pathland-render-qt)",
            )
        nativeQt = Native.load(libraryPath, NativeQtRenderer::class.java)
    }

    /**
     * Set the directory that web-style `/_pathland/...` media/image source paths
     * resolve against. Call before [runRing]; an empty value clears it.
     */
    fun setAssetRoot(dir: String) {
        nativeQt.pathland_qt_set_asset_root(dir)
    }

    /**
     * Run the Qt renderer over the borrowed ring. Blocks until the Qt event loop
     * exits. On macOS the JVM must run with `-XstartOnFirstThread`.
     */
    fun runRing(ring: Pointer, onEvent: EventCallback?, width: Int, height: Int) {
        nativeQt.pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, onEvent, width, height)
    }

    companion object {
        private val INSTANCE: QtRendererNative by lazy { QtRendererNative() }

        /** The process-wide binding; lazily links `libpathland_qt` on first call. */
        fun instance(): QtRendererNative = INSTANCE

        /** Resolve the native library's full path (system property, then `java.library.path`). */
        internal fun resolveLibraryPath(): String? {
            val override = System.getProperty("pathland.qt.lib")
            if (override != null) return override
            val fileName = "libpathland_qt" + platformLibraryExtension()
            val libraryPath = System.getProperty("java.library.path") ?: return null
            for (dir in libraryPath.split(File.pathSeparator)) {
                val candidate = File(dir, fileName)
                if (candidate.isFile) return candidate.absolutePath
            }
            return null
        }

        private fun platformLibraryExtension(): String {
            val os = System.getProperty("os.name", "").lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
            if (os.contains("mac")) return ".dylib"
            if (os.contains("win")) return ".dll"
            return ".so"
        }
    }
}

# pathland-gtk-demo (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

Runs the shared Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` (`dev.pathland.demo.music` from
`pathland-demo-views-kotlin`) under the **native GTK4 renderer**
(`libpathland_gtk`) — the cross-language, shared-renderer story for Java. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## How it works

- The Kotlin DSL mounts the view through its fine-grained `Emitter` into a
  `libpathland_core` shared ring (`RingOpcodeSink`, **zero-copy**).
- The in-process GTK renderer pumps the same ring in place
  (`pathland_gtk_run_ring`, via `PathlandCore.ringMut`); no
  `pathland-view-native` host is involved.
- Native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that this host drains
  (`pathland_core_drain_events`) and dispatches into the app's bindings via the
  shared `InputDispatcher` (taps, text/value/date inputs, **media events**,
  router back).
- State/theme/platform seeding mirrors the server session: `PersistentState`
  over an `InMemoryStateStore`, `DemoTheme.adaptive()` as the emitter theme.
- **App-driven media**: the renderer plays the demo's tracks through a direct
  GStreamer `playbin` (driven by the node's media control properties) and
  reports `MEDIA_*` events back through the ring. The app's web-style
  `/_pathland/assets/...` paths are resolved against a local asset root: the
  demo extracts its audio + covers from the shared `pathland-demo-common` jar at
  startup (`DemoAssets.extractToTemp`) and calls `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`.

## Implemented

- `GtkRendererNative` — JNA binding to `libpathland_gtk`
  (`pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` +
  `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root(dir)`); library resolved from the
  `pathland.gtk.lib` system property or `java.library.path`.
- `RingEventReader` — decodes raw ring `EVENT` opcodes into
  `dev.pathland.view.core.transport.Event`, resolving `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE`
  strings from the shared host → guest event arena (header `0x40`), plus the
  `MEDIA_*` events (play state, time, ended, volume, duration) and
  `FIT_CHANGED` (routed to the emitter's fit sink, so the `SizeThatFits` slot
  swaps to its wide candidate and the now-playing sidebar appears). Headless
  unit tests cover pointer/value/date/text/navigate/media/fit decoding and
  bounds behaviour.
- `GtkHost` (`main`) — mounts `MusicPlayerView` (the Apple Music-style player:
  library, now-playing sidebar, player bar with transport/seek/volume), extracts
  the demo's audio + covers to a runtime dir, sets the asset root, runs GTK
  (1180×800), drains and dispatches events. Blocks until the window closes.
- The `Emitter` sets `BINDING_ID` on bound controls for `RingOpcodeSink`s (the
  GTK renderer gates `TEXT_CHANGED`/`VALUE_CHANGED` on it).

## Not implemented / gaps

- **Playback requires GStreamer** with the mp3 decoding plugins installed (the
  brew `gstreamer` formula bundles them); without it the app runs but the
  pipeline errors on play.
- The GTK renderer's `attach_control_events` covers `TOGGLE`/`SLIDER`/
  `TEXT_FIELD`/`PICKER` only: `DATE_PICKER`, `STEPPER`, `COLOR_PICKER`, and
  `TEXT_EDITOR` render but do not (yet) emit events under GTK.
- macOS requires `-XstartOnFirstThread` (GTK owns the main thread).
- No automated GUI test (headless renderer tests live in `pathland-render-gtk`).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-gtk-demo` — `RingEventReaderTest` (6 tests, headless, no
GTK). Manual: `GtkHost` boots the window and renders `MusicPlayerView` via the
shared ring; with GStreamer installed the pipeline reaches `PLAYING` and reports
`MEDIA_*` events (verified with a seeded `playing=true` run + `GST_DEBUG`). The
full Java reactor compiles with this module.===== QT STATUS

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

Fully Kotlin JNA desktop demo: the shared Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` under the native
Qt Quick renderer (`libpathland_qt`), over the `libpathland_core` shared ring.

`scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh`.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
        <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
        <version>0.1.5</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <!-- Demo application — not published to Maven Central. -->
    <properties>
        <maven.deploy.skip>true</maven.deploy.skip>
        <maven.javadoc.skip>true</maven.javadoc.skip>
        <!-- Quarkus 3.39.1 manages Kotlin 2.4.10; inherit the reactor's compiler. -->
    </properties>

    <name>Pathland Quarkus Kotlin Demo</name>
    <description>
        Kotlin Quarkus demonstration app: SSR plus live 16-byte opcode deltas over
        WebSocket, authored entirely through pathland-view-kotlin and the Kotlin DSL
        Quarkus extension. It deliberately does not depend on the Java DSL or the
        shared Java demo views.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-quarkus-kotlin</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view-kotlin</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-demo-views-kotlin</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-junit</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <sourceDirectory>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</sourceDirectory>
        <testSourceDirectory>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</testSourceDirectory>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <argLine>-Dpathland.proxy.snapshot-timeout-ms=10000</argLine>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>compile</id>
                        <phase>process-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>test-compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <compilerPlugins>
                        <plugin>all-open</plugin>
                    </compilerPlugins>
                    <pluginOptions>
                        <option>all-open:annotation=jakarta.enterprise.context.ApplicationScoped</option>
                        <option>all-open:annotation=jakarta.enterprise.context.Dependent</option>
                        <option>all-open:annotation=jakarta.inject.Singleton</option>
                        <option>all-open:annotation=jakarta.ws.rs.Path</option>
                    </pluginOptions>
                </configuration>
                <dependencies>
                    <dependency>
                        <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                        <artifactId>kotlin-maven-allopen</artifactId>
                        <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                    </dependency>
                </dependencies>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
                <artifactId>quarkus-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>

/**
 * A small Kotlin-owned view that exercises persisted state, two-way text input,
 * reactive plain-Kotlin control flow, `ForEach`, and the Kotlin modifier sugar.
 */
class KotlinDemoView : Component() {

    private var count by state(0)
    private val name = mutableState("", "demo.name")
    private var items by state(listOf("First item", "Second item"))

    override fun body(): View = VStack(spacing = 16f) {
        Text("Pathland Kotlin Demo")
            .fontSize(28f)
            .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)
        Text("SSR plus live 16-byte opcode deltas, authored in Kotlin.")

        HStack(spacing = 12f) {
            Text("Count: $count")
            Button("Increment") { count += 1 }
            Button("Reset") { count = 0 }
        }

        TextField("Your name", name)
        Text(computed { "Hello, ${name.value.ifBlank { "world" }}" })

        HStack(spacing = 12f) {
            Button("Add item") { items = items + "Item ${items.size + 1}" }
            Button("Clear items") { items = emptyList() }
        }

        ForEach(items) { item, _ -> Text("• $item") }
    }.padding(24).frame { maxWidth(720f) }
}

package dev.pathland.demo.quarkus.kotlin

import io.quarkus.test.common.http.TestHTTPResource
import io.quarkus.test.junit.QuarkusTest
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertFalse
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertNotNull
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
import java.net.URI
import java.net.URL
import java.net.http.HttpClient
import java.net.http.HttpRequest
import java.net.http.HttpResponse

/** The Kotlin app boots, its CDI bean is discovered, and SSR renders the Kotlin tree. */
@QuarkusTest
class KotlinDemoSmokeTest {

    @TestHTTPResource("/")
    lateinit var base: URL

    @Test
    fun ssrRendersTheKotlinDemo() {
        val response = get("/")

        assertEquals(200, response.statusCode())
        assertTrue(response.body().contains("Library"), response.body())
        assertTrue(response.body().contains("Building on Solid Ground"), response.body())
        assertTrue(response.body().contains("8 songs · 8 albums"), response.body())
        assertTrue(response.body().contains("Pathland · Building on Solid Ground"), response.body())
    }

    @Test
    fun adViewIsMountedAndEmbeddedThroughTheProxy() {
        // Warm the mounted origin first: the first cold Kotlin view render can be slow on
        // CI, and the proxy's SSR snapshot budget starts only after the parent mounts.
        val ad = get("/ad")
        assertEquals(200, ad.statusCode(), "the ad app is mounted at /ad")
        assertTrue(ad.body().contains("Pathland Ads"), "the ad app renders directly at /ad")

        val html = get("/").body()
        assertTrue(html.contains("Pathland Ads"), "the proxied ad app's title is embedded: $html")
        assertTrue(html.contains("Clicked 0 times"), "the ad app's counter renders through the proxy")
        assertTrue(html.contains("data-pathland-id=\"1073741825\""),
            "the ad subtree carries remapped ids from the proxy range")
    }

    @Test
    fun ssrServesTheContentHashedDomBundle() {
        val html = get("/").body()
        assertFalse(html.contains("/_pathland/dom-renderer.js\""),
                "the pre-hash fallback must not be emitted when the app manifest is visible")

        val src = Regex("""src="(/_pathland/dom-renderer-[^"]+\.js)"""")
            .find(html)?.groupValues?.get(1)
        assertNotNull(src, "the SSR document references the content-hashed DOM bundle: $html")

        val bundle = get(src!!)
        assertEquals(200, bundle.statusCode(), "GET $src")
        assertTrue(bundle.headers().firstValue("Content-Type").orElse("")
                .startsWith("text/javascript"), "served as JavaScript")
    }

    private fun get(path: String): HttpResponse<String> =
        HttpClient.newHttpClient().send(
            HttpRequest.newBuilder(URI.create(base.toString()).resolve(path)).GET().build(),
            HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString(),
        )
}

# pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

Kotlin-first Quarkus demo: SSR plus live 16-byte opcode deltas over WebSocket,
authored with `pathland-view-kotlin` and hosted by `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`.

## Implemented

- Kotlin `PathlandApp` CDI bean (`KotlinDemoApplication`) mounting the Kotlin
  `MusicPlayerView` at `/`.
- **Sponsored proxy** — a second `MountedApp` at `/ad` (`AdView`), embedded into
  the player's Now Playing pane via `ProxyView` (same-server loopback proxy).
- The standalone `KotlinDemoView` remains available as a small state/input
  showcase.
- Exercises persisted state (`count`, `items`), two-way text input (`name`),
  reactive computed text, `ForEach`, and Kotlin modifier sugar.
- Quarkus Kotlin build setup: `kotlin-maven-plugin`, `all-open` for CDI/JAX-RS
  annotations, `jvmTarget=17`.
- The removed Java DSL (`pathland-view`) and Java demo views are not on the
  classpath: the demo is
  Kotlin-DSL-only.
- `KotlinDemoSmokeTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts the CDI bean is discovered, SSR
  renders the Kotlin tree, the `/ad` app is mounted and embedded through the proxy
  (with remapped proxy ids), and the SSR document references the content-hashed
  DOM bundle (a GET on that URL returns 200).
- The DOM renderer bundle + service worker are copied by
  `lib/typescript/scripts/copy-to-demos.mjs`.
- Run with `scripts/run-quarkus-kotlin-demo.sh` → `http://localhost:8080`.

## Not implemented / gaps

- No WebSocket delta integration test yet; SSR discovery is covered.
- No Quarkus codestart yet.
- Native image is not supported (Rust HTML renderer via JNA).

- **Observability seam** — `PathlandTelemetry` (default `NOOP`): the runtime emits
  session open/close, inbound event batches, flushed batches (frames/opcodes/bytes +
  merge-encode time), SSR render latency, resync requests, and send failures; the host

  the starters auto-wire them. Logging is **SLF4J** (both frameworks bind it) — the old
  ad-hoc `System.out` is gone. See issue #62.
- **Concurrency stress** — `RegistryConcurrencyTest`: 100 sessions driven through the
  registry concurrently (clicks on each session's button) while SSR-style requests
  construct throwaway sessions on request threads — the shared-actor / global-`Scheduler`
  cross-session corruption guard. Each session must reach exactly its own click count
  (no lost effects, no cross-session values).
- **Shared WS test harness** — `dev.pathland.server.test.{WsSession,MultiSessionProbe}`
  (a JDK-WebSocket client speaking the PLPL protocol: env/resync/click/ping) lives in the
  **`pathland-test-kit`** module (main scope, so package builds resolve it as a normal
  jar); the starters' 100-session stress tests reuse it.
- **`StateStores`** — default state store: Redis when reachable, else the supplied
  fallback.
- **SSR debug comments (property-gated)**: `PathlandSession`/`PathlandRegistry` take a
  `debugHtml` flag (constructor + `isDebugHtml()`); when set, `renderHtml` uses the
  renderer's debug mode so every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming
  its component and the modifiers applied. The Spring/Quarkus starters bind it to the
  `pathland.debug-html` property (default `false`).
- **Reserved framework root**: `PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE` (`/_pathland`) — the
  SSR page carries the app's base as `data-pathland-base` and the DOM-client bundle is
  injected at `{base}/dom-renderer-<sha256>.js` (`PathlandAssets` reads the current
  name from the `_pathland/dom-renderer.current` manifest on the classpath, resolving
  through the thread context classloader first so a Quarkus extension parent loader
  can see the application's static resources; it falls back to the literal
  `dom-renderer.js` only when absent) so the client's WebSocket and
  asset refs resolve from the same reserved prefix (spec DSL.md). The content-hashed

  base design is linked the same way: `renderHtml` renders through

  `{base}/base-<sha256>.css` (token overrides/fit rules stay inline).

# pathland-view-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

The sole JVM authoring surface (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`), Kotlin-owned over the
Kotlin `pathland-view-core`. The Java DSL, its processor, and its Java-only
Quarkus extension/starter alias are removed.

## Authoring surface

- **Kotlin-owned**: all primitives, shapes, stacks, grids, scroll/lazy
  containers, `ForEach`, `Button`, text/value controls, media, navigation,
  `Label`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`, `ProxyView`, styles (`PlainButtonStyle`,
  `BorderedButtonStyle`, label styles, `NativeVideoStyle`), and the complete
  modifier vocabulary (padding/frame/fonts/colors/borders/shadows/effects/
  transforms/interaction/accessibility/environment/styles/window metadata).
- **Dependency boundary**: main depends on `pathland-view-core` only.
- Tests are Kotlin-only; golden engine traces and opcode/property assertions
  replace the former Java-vs-Kotlin parity oracle.

## Implemented

- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`, `Rectangle`,
  `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`,
  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
- **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
  `ProxyView`.
- **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
  `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
  `ColorPicker`.
- **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
  `.children(...)`. A custom `Component` constructed inline in a block
  auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`
  inside `body()` (it does not leak into the enclosing scope). An explicit
  `view.add()` / `+view` is available for Java-constructed or prebuilt views.
- **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
  `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`, `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
- **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
  layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
  foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
  visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
  environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents. A child
  modifier replaces its auto-registered leaf in the enclosing builder, so
  `VStack { Text("x").fontSize(20f) }` keeps the modifier. The core
  `View.modifiers(...)` operation remains available as an escape hatch.
- **Persisted state**: `Component` base class + `val count by state(0)`
  (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
  form for two-way controls. Bound to the session's `PersistentState` before the
  first `body()` render — no kapt and no annotation processor.
- **`Signals.state`**: Components and services can create persisted signals with
  `Signals.state("key", initial)` while the framework's session state is active
  during render. Outside a state context it falls back to an in-memory signal.
- **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
  list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
- **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
  `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
- **Media**: `Video(controller)` stays where the app places it; audio remains
  view-less. `controller.register()` projects a controller at the root (ordinary
  audio services call it while rendering).
- **Tests**: structure/opcode/property assertions, auto-collection,
  child-modifier application, modifier property parity, fine-grained signal
  deltas, persisted/stateful bodies, reactive `ForEach`, two-way
  `TextField`/`Slider`/`Stepper`, navigation swaps and link intents, and media
  projection (audio root nodes,
  authored `VIDEO` placement, stable controller ids, and late nested videos).

## Naming

- The composite base is `Component` (renamed from `KotlinView` now that the Java
  DSL is gone). Whether to align the authoring type with SwiftUI's single `View`
  protocol is tracked by #174.

## Java hosting

- A Java Spring Boot / Quarkus app mounts a Kotlin view through the Java-friendly
  `PathlandApp` functional interface (`return () -> MusicPlayerView.make();`).
- Kotlin root views expose public constructors and/or `@JvmStatic make(...)`
  factories with Java-friendly parameter types.
- Tests in `pathland-spring-boot-starter` and `pathland-quarkus` prove a Java
  host renders a Kotlin fixture and receives live signal deltas.

## Not implemented / gaps

- No Kotlin Multiplatform target yet — the module is JVM-only over
  `pathland-view-core`.
- `SecureField` is Kotlin-owned (`TEXT_FIELD` + `IS_SECURE`).

# pathland-view-core (JVM engine) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine and runtime for the Pathland protocol,
now written entirely in Kotlin. It owns the `View` SPI and shared authoring
vocabulary, the retained-tree diff emitter, signals/computed/effects, the wire
codec, router, cross-platform state, and JNA ring interop. `pathland-view-kotlin`
is the sole authoring layer; server and renderer modules depend on core only.
Java hosts consume the same API through Kotlin/JVM interop.

## Implemented

- **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`,
  `Commands`, `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`, `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`,
  `TokenPath`.
- **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`state`/`computed`/
  `effect`/`untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
  caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
  `Scheduler`. `Signals.state` binds to the ambient session `PersistentState`
  during a component render.
- **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `PersistentState`, untyped
  `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Kotlin `Component` state delegates
  bind directly before `body()`; the Java `State` field/binder machinery and
  annotation processor are removed.
- **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`,
  `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`.
- **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
  `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
  `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` and the navigation helpers live in the Kotlin DSL.
- **JNA interop** (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`): lazy `PathlandCore` binding and
  `RingOpcodeSink` over `libpathland_core`.
- **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
  `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
  Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
  effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
  zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract. Registered `MediaController`s are
  projected as pinned, non-visual root children; `unregisterMediaController`
  removes them without touching the app tree.
- **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
  `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`,
  `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
  `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
  wrappers.
- **Protocol manifest validation** (`ProtocolManifestTest`): the hand-written
  protocol constants (`Components`, `Properties`, `Commands`, `Categories`,
  `ValueTypes`) are checked against `spec/protocol.tsv` — including no extra
  public numeric constants and the full `ValueTypes.forProperty` mapping. No
  Java source is generated.
- **Shared engine traces**: the Kotlin DSL tests run the mount/text/property
  scenarios against the Rust-emitted PLPL fixtures under `spec/engine-traces/`,
  byte-for-byte. The canonical order lives in `spec/ENGINE.md`.
- **Tests**: `pathland-view-core` owns the signal, state, frame-codec, and
  protocol-manifest tests; Kotlin DSL tests exercise the emitter end-to-end, and
  the server/HTML/desktop consumers cover their integration paths.

## Package boundary

- `pathland-view-core` is one Maven module for now: `core`/`engine` are logical
  subpackages inside it, with a few deliberate intra-module references
  (`Color`/`MediaController`/`Modified` materialize `PathlandNode`). Splitting
  `core` and `engine` into separate artifacts requires a node SPI first.
- Production runtimes/renderers (`pathland-server-core`,
  `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-test-kit`) depend on
  core. Java-module tests add `pathland-view-kotlin` in test scope and mount
  Kotlin-authored fixture views; production starters remain DSL-neutral.

     linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64.
    - `java` — set the version, stage the natives into the renderer jar, run
      `mvn -P release deploy` to Maven Central (auto-published after validation).
    - `bump` — commit the version back to `main`.
    - `release-assets` — attach the `.crate` files, the Java main jars, and the
      four native libs to the GitHub Release.

The Java deploy runs on **Maven 3.9.9** (pinned in the workflow): Maven 3.10
writes a `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
which the Portal rejects ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). The demos
are **excluded from the release reactor** (`-pl '!pathland-demo-common,!pathland-demo-views-kotlin,!pathland-gtk-demo,!pathland-qt-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'`)
— `central-publishing-maven-plugin` bundles every reactor module, ignoring
`maven.deploy.skip`, and the demos must not be published.

The publish steps are **idempotent**: a crate+version already on crates.io is
skipped, so re-running a partially failed release is safe (re-run the workflow
via `workflow_dispatch`, passing the `tag`). Maven Central rejects a re-deploy of
an existing version, so a Java re-run only helps if the Java deploy did not
complete.

- **Only changes are sent.** A screen that isn't changing transmits zero bytes.
  Updates are tiny binary deltas, not re-rendered pages or JSON trees.
- **Native elements, not a canvas.** The platform lays out and animates real
  elements — you get native layout, text rendering, and accessibility for free,
  whether those elements are DOM nodes or GTK widgets.
- **A thin client.** The web client is a small static file that hydrates the server
  HTML and applies updates in place. No framework, no virtual DOM, no re-render cost.

resources. It's shipped, not maintained — all the real logic lives in your backend.

### 9.4 Conformance recipe

A generated DSL is verified by proving it **emits the same bytes** as the
reference implementations:

1. Port the golden vectors in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) into the new

   opcodes for each canonical element.
2. Port the Java `EmitterTest` cases (mount → `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE`
   deltas; unchanged tree → zero opcodes; two-way routing: `TEXT_CHANGED`,

3. Verify the no-heap-allocation steady-state property where the target
   language supports it (the Rust engine proves zero dynamic allocations during
   steady-state emission).
4. Cross-check every referenced id against PRIMITIVES.md/MODIFIERS.md/EVENTS.md

  delivered through a side-channel callback — they flow through the opcode engine.

controllers (`Button::clicked` → pointer up, `EventControllerMotion` →

Done on branch `refactor/consolidate-maven-modules`.

**19 → 10 Maven modules**
- `pathland-view-core` absorbs `pathland-view-kotlin`
- `pathland-server-core` absorbs `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-observability`, `pathland-test-kit`
- `pathland-quarkus` absorbs `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`; `pathland-quarkus-deployment` absorbs `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment`
- `pathland-demo-views-kotlin` absorbs `pathland-demo-common`
- `pathland-desktop-demo` merges the GTK + Qt demos (shared `RingEventReader`)
- `pathland-quarkus-demo` absorbs the Kotlin demo as a mounted `/kotlin` app

Also updated root/CI/release configs, scripts, docs, `AGENTS.md`, and merged/deleted the affected `status.md` files.

**Verification**
- `cd lib/rust && cargo build -p pathland-render-html` — ok
- `cd lib/java && mvn -q -B clean install` — success; all surefire suites green (view-core 61, server-core 71, render-html 12, demos/starter/quarkus ok)
- Quarkus demo shows both `pathland` and `pathland-kotlin` features installed
- Repo-wide grep finds no references to the removed artifact IDs

Changes are staged but **not committed**.
